cohort: The study included 50 pregnant women, with 25 women having a BMI > 25 (cases) and 25 women having a normal BMI (controls).
finding: Maternal BMI shows strong associations with pregnancy complications and outcome, with both maternal (e.g., pre-eclampsia, induced labor, cesarean section) and fetal complications (e.g., pre-term labor, macrosomia, low APGAR score, fetal distress) being increased in the high BMI group.
mod_finding: The obese group experienced a two-fold increase in induced labours and a three-fold increase in caesarean section rates compared to the normal BMI group.
